cards.explanation: The answer is God's mercy. Paul says he urges them “…on account of God’s mercy…” He starts with what God has shown them before he asks them for anything. I think that's why the ask lands softer than a to-do list taped to the oven door.

The answer is bodies. Paul asks them to offer their bodies as living sacrifices. That means the whole you, the one that walks, works and shows up. I only ever offered dough to the oven, friends, so this is a bigger deal than anything on my counter.

The answer is True. Paul says offering your bodies as living sacrifices is “…your spiritual service of worship.” He ties worship to the body, not just the singing. That's the word to hold onto, friends.

The answer is transformed. Paul says not to be conformed to this world, “…but be transformed by the renewing of your mind.” The transforming happens by the renewing of the mind. I know a little about being made over, friends. Mine came with a brand new apron.

The answer is God's will. Paul says that with a renewed mind, “Then you will be able to test and approve what is the good, pleasing, and perfect will of God.” Notice it's a will you can test and approve. That's a lot better than guessing at a recipe with the card missing.

The answer is thinking too highly of themselves. Paul says to every one of them, “Do not think of yourself more highly than you ought…” He says it to every one of them, not just a few. I've dived face-first into chocolate chips and called it graceful. Nobody gave me a score, friends, and I still gave myself a ten.

The answer is God. Paul says to think of yourself with sober judgment, “…according to the measure of faith God has given you.” The giver is God, and the faith is given to you, friends. That's a gift you can hold with a humble heart.
The answer is body. Paul says that “…in Christ we who are many are one body…” Many people, one body. It's like a whole kitchen crew pulling off one big batch, and nobody is the whole kitchen alone.
The answer is False. Paul says, “…each member belongs to one another.” Nobody belongs only to themselves. That's a lot of belonging, and I think it's good news for anyone who's felt alone.

The answer is False, and Paul says so himself: “We have different gifts according to the grace given us.” Then he starts listing them, one by one. If everybody had the same gift, it'd be like a kitchen with fifty rolling pins and not one oven mitt. Somebody's getting burned, friends.
The answer is True. Paul says, “…let him lead with diligence…” That one's for whoever is out front. Leading isn't a break from work, friends. It has work built in.
The answer is cheerfully. Paul says, “…let him do it cheerfully.” Mercy handed over with a smile. It's the kind of thing I'd stamp on every cookie box if I could fit it.
